title: A thousand elephants
hookLine: Andal dreams her wedding to the Lord, step by step, and families still sing it to bless their own weddings
carry: the soul's wedding to god blesses ours
last: BHAKTI LONGS TO BE NEAR GOD.

cards: Friend, I had a dream. That's roughly how the song begins, and what follows is a wedding. Elephants first, a thousand of them, the song says, circling round as the groom comes into town.
Then the canopy, the drums, the bride's hand taken, the walk around the fire. Every detail is there, the way you'd tell your closest friend the morning after a dream you can't shake.
The dreamer is Andal, and the groom is the Lord. Our last day with her: the dream, and the ending tradition gives her.

teach.b: The song is the sixth in the Nachiyar Tirumoli, named for its opening words, Varanam Ayiram, a thousand elephants.
In paraphrase, each verse is one moment of the wedding, and each closes with something like, I dreamed it, friend. The town is decorated. A pavilion goes up, hung with pearls.
The groom arrives. The relatives gather; the bride is dressed. He takes her hand.
They walk around the sacred fire together. He sets her foot on the grinding stone, one of the steps of the rite. It's a full Tamil wedding, told from the inside, by a bride who hasn't had one.
Here's the teaching inside the song.

teach.h: THE LORD AS THE SOUL'S BELOVED
teach.b: In Sri Vaishnava devotion the Lord is the soul's true beloved, and Andal is the bride every soul is meant to be.
So some Sri Vaishnava families sing Varanam Ayiram at their own weddings, and many read it as setting an ordinary marriage inside that bigger one: two people blessed by the soul's wedding to God.
Then the ending, as tradition tells it. Her father, Periyalvar, worries: whom can she marry? The story says the Lord of the temple at Srirangam lets it be known that he will take her.
So her father brings her there, dressed as a bride.

teach.h: THE BRIDE WHO WALKED INTO THE SHRINE
teach.b: She walks into the shrine, toward the reclining image of the Lord, and isn't seen again. Tradition says she became one with him. The texts are her songs; the ending is the story her community tells.
In her poems, the wedding stays a dream.

how: Some Sri Vaishnava families sing Andal's Varanam Ayiram at weddings, and celebrate her marriage to the Lord at her temple in Srivilliputtur and at Srirangam.

games.q: you're Periyalvar. your daughter will marry no one but the Lord, and word comes that the Lord of Srirangam will take her. what do you do?
o: keep her home, and hope she changes her mind.
bring her to Srirangam, dressed as a bride.
games.why: in the story, he brings her to the temple as a bride. she walks into the shrine and isn't seen again; tradition says she became one with the Lord.

practice: Bring to mind a couple you love, married, engaged or long together. At Hindu weddings, guests toss grains of rice, akshata, over the couple as a blessing.

Picture them in front of you, and in your mind let a handful of rice fall over them, slowly, with a wish for their life together. Stay with that picture for a few breaths. If you pray, ask God's blessing on them.
If you don't, simply wish them well.
